23: 	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
24: 	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
25: 	"golang.org/x/term"
26: )

28: func (c *CLab) Destroy(ctx context.Context, options ...DestroyOption) (err error) {
29: 	opts := NewDestroyOptions()
30: 
31: 	for _, opt := range options {
32: 		opt(opts)
33: 	}
34: 
35: 	if c.LabRuntime != nil {
36: 		return c.destroyWithLabRuntime(ctx, opts)
37: 	}
38: 
39: 	var containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer
40: 
41: 	switch {
42: 	case opts.all:
43: 		containers, err = c.ListContainers(ctx)
44: 	case c.TopoPaths.TopologyFilenameAbsPath() != "":
45: 		containers, err = c.ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound(ctx)
46: 		if err == nil {
47: 			var tailscaleContainers []clabruntime.GenericContainer
48: 			tailscaleContainers, err = c.discoverTailscaleContainers(ctx, opts.nodeFilter)
49: 			containers = append(containers, tailscaleContainers...)
50: 		}
51: 	default:
52: 		var listOpts []ListOption
53: 
54: 		if c.Config.Name != "" {
55: 			listOpts = []ListOption{WithListLabName(c.Config.Name)}
56: 		} else {
57: 			listOpts = []ListOption{WithListclabLabelExists()}
58: 		}
59: 
60: 		containers, err = c.ListContainers(ctx, listOpts...)
61: 	}
62: 
63: 	if err != nil {
64: 		return err
65: 	}
66: 
67: 	// topo will hold the reference to the topology file
68: 	// as the key and the respective lab directory as the referenced value
69: 	topos := map[string]string{}
70: 
71: 	for idx := range containers {
72: 		topoFile, ok := containers[idx].Labels[clabconstants.TopoFile]
73: 		if !ok {
74: 			continue
75: 		}
76: 
77: 		topos[topoFile] = filepath.Dir(containers[idx].Labels[clabconstants.NodeLabDir])
78: 	}
79: 
80: 	// failedLabDirs records the lab directories whose destroy failed or was never
81: 	// attempted. --cleanup keeps those directories: deleting the lab directory of
82: 	// a lab that is still running would discard the state file destroy needs for
83: 	// its management network cleanup on the next attempt.
84: 	failedLabDirs := map[string]bool{}
85: 
86: 	defer func() {
87: 		if opts.cleanup {
88: 			if cleanupErr := c.destroyLabDirs(topos, opts.all, failedLabDirs); cleanupErr != nil {
89: 				err = errors.Join(err, cleanupErr)
90: 			}
91: 		}
92: 	}()
93: 
94: 	if len(topos) == 0 {
95: 		return nil
96: 	}
97: 
98: 	log.Debugf("got the following topologies for destroy: %+v", topos)
99: 
100: 	// if all, and cli doesn't have --yes flag, and in a terminal -- prompt user confirmation
101: 	if opts.all && opts.terminalPrompt && term.IsTerminal(int(os.Stdin.Fd())) {
102: 		err := cliPromptToDestroyAll(topos)
103: 		if err != nil {
104: 			return err
105: 		}
106: 	}
107: 
108: 	var errs []error
109: 
110: 	for topo, labDir := range topos {
111: 		cc, err := c.makeCopyForDestroy(ctx, topo, labDir, *opts)
112: 		if err != nil {
113: 			log.Errorf("error creating clab instance for topo %q: %v", topo, err)
114: 
115: 			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf(
116: 				"error creating clab instance for topo %q: %w", topo, err))
117: 			failedLabDirs[labDir] = true
118: 
119: 			continue
120: 		}
121: 
122: 		err = cc.destroy(ctx, opts.maxWorkers, opts.keepMgmtNet)
123: 		if err != nil {
124: 			log.Errorf("Error occurred during the %s lab deletion: %v", cc.Config.Name, err)
125: 			errs = append(errs, err)
126: 			failedLabDirs[labDir] = true
127: 		}
128: 	}
129: 
130: 	if len(errs) != 0 {
131: 		return fmt.Errorf("error(s) occurred during the deletion. Check log messages")
132: 	}
133: 
134: 	return nil
135: }

137: // creates a mostly cloned version of the current c but set to the new topology, and with the
138: // necessary steps (mgmt network things) handled preparing the new CLab for destruction.
139: func (c *CLab) makeCopyForDestroy(
140: 	ctx context.Context,
141: 	topo,
142: 	labDir string,
143: 	opts DestroyOptions,
144: ) (*CLab, error) {
145: 	newOpts := []ClabOption{
146: 		WithTimeout(c.timeout),
147: 		// a topology edited after deploy may no longer pass the mgmt-net link checks,
148: 		// which must not prevent the removal of the deployed lab.
149: 		WithSkippedMgmtNetLinksCheck(),
150: 	}
151: 
152: 	// Try to load topology file if it exists, otherwise use lab name only.
153: 	// This allows destroying labs even when the topology file has been deleted.
154: 	// WithTopoPath / WithLabNameOnly must run before WithNodeFilter so filterClabNodes
155: 	// sees topology nodes (see filterClabNodes in clab.go).
156: 	varsFiles := opts.varsFiles
157: 	if len(varsFiles) == 0 {
158: 		varsFiles = c.TopoPaths.VarsFilenamesAbsPath()
159: 	}
160: 
161: 	if clabutils.FileOrDirExists(topo) {
162: 		newOpts = append(newOpts, WithTopoPath(topo, varsFiles))
163: 	} else {
164: 		// Derive lab name from lab directory (format: clab-<labname>)
165: 		labName := filepath.Base(labDir)
166: 		labName = strings.TrimPrefix(labName, "clab-")
167: 		log.Debugf("topology file %q not found, using lab name %q for destroy", topo, labName)
168: 		newOpts = append(newOpts, WithLabNameOnly(labName))
169: 	}
170: 
171: 	newOpts = append(newOpts,
172: 		WithNodeFilter(opts.nodeFilter),
173: 		// during destroy we don't want to check bind paths
174: 		// as it is irrelevant for this command.
175: 		WithSkippedBindsPathsCheck(),
176: 		WithRuntime(
177: 			c.globalRuntimeName,
178: 			&clabruntime.RuntimeConfig{
179: 				Debug:            c.Config.Debug,
180: 				Timeout:          c.timeout,
181: 				GracefulShutdown: opts.graceful,
182: 			},
183: 		),
184: 	)
185: 
186: 	if opts.keepMgmtNet {
187: 		newOpts = append(newOpts, WithKeepMgmtNet())
188: 	}
189: 
190: 	cc, err := NewContainerLab(newOpts...)
191: 	if err != nil {
192: 		return nil, err
193: 	}
194: 	if labDir != "" && clabutils.FileOrDirExists(labDir) {
195: 		// adjust the labdir. Usually we take the PWD. but now on destroy time,
196: 		// we might be in a different Dir.
197: 		err = cc.TopoPaths.SetLabDir(labDir)
198: 		if err != nil {
199: 			return nil, err
200: 		}
201: 	}
202: 
203: 	// populate the management network state (bridge names) destroy needs for the
204: 	// removal of the iptables rules, without creating networks that are missing:
205: 	// a lab deployed with a management network override leaves the topology's
206: 	// default network uncreated, and creating it here would collide with the
207: 	// subnets the override is using.
208: 	if !cc.mgmtNetworksSkipped() {
209: 		var bridged clabtypes.MgmtNetworks
210: 		for _, m := range cc.allMgmtNetworks() {
211: 			if m.Driver != clabtypes.MgmtDriverMacvlan {
212: 				bridged = append(bridged, m)
213: 			}
214: 		}
215: 		if err = cc.resolveExistingMgmtNetworks(ctx, bridged); err != nil {
216: 			return nil, err
217: 		}
218: 	}
219: 
220: 	err = cc.setMgmtNetLinkBridges()
221: 	if err != nil {
222: 		return nil, err
223: 	}
224: 
225: 	err = cc.ResolveLinks()
226: 	if err != nil {
227: 		return nil, err
228: 	}
229: 
230: 	return cc, nil
231: }
232: 
233: // resolveExistingMgmtNetworks inspects the management networks that already exist
234: // so their bridge names are populated, e.g. for the iptables cleanup on destroy.
235: // Networks that do not exist are skipped: they hold no bridge yet, and the callers
236: // must not create management networks. Runtimes that cannot check network existence
237: // keep the create-or-inspect behavior.
238: func (c *CLab) resolveExistingMgmtNetworks(
239: 	ctx context.Context,
240: 	networks clabtypes.MgmtNetworks,
241: ) error {
242: 	var existing clabtypes.MgmtNetworks
243: 
244: 	for _, m := range networks {
245: 		rt, rtErr := c.mgmtRuntime(c.globalRuntimeName, m)
246: 		if rtErr != nil {
247: 			// runtimes without multiple network support never created extra networks
248: 			log.Debug(
249: 				"Skipping management network resolution", "network", m.Network, "error", rtErr,
250: 			)
251: 			continue
252: 		}
253: 
254: 		checker, ok := rt.(clabruntime.MgmtNetworkChecker)
255: 		if !ok {
256: 			existing = append(existing, m)
257: 			continue
258: 		}
259: 
260: 		exists, err := checker.MgmtNetworkExists(ctx)
261: 		if err != nil {
262: 			return err
263: 		}
264: 		if !exists {
265: 			log.Debug("Skipping management network that does not exist", "network", m.Network)
266: 			continue
267: 		}
268: 
269: 		existing = append(existing, m)
270: 	}
271: 
272: 	return c.createNetworks(ctx, existing)
273: }

275: // destroyLabDirs removes the lab directories of the destroyed labs. Directories
276: // recorded in failedLabDirs are kept: their labs are still running, and the
277: // directory holds the lab state a later destroy attempt relies on.
278: func (c *CLab) destroyLabDirs(
279: 	topos map[string]string,
280: 	all bool,
281: 	failedLabDirs map[string]bool,
282: ) error {
283: 	if len(topos) == 0 {
284: 		log.Info("no containerlab containers found")
285: 
286: 		if !all {
287: 			labDir := c.TopoPaths.TopologyLabDir()
288: 			if labDir == "" {
289: 				// Try to infer the precise lab directory when TopologyLabDir is not set,
290: 				// e.g. destroy --name without topology file. Only look for an exact
291: 				// clab-<name> match, never a wildcard.
292: 				if c.Config != nil && c.Config.Name != "" {
293: 					candidates := []string{}
294: 					if base := os.Getenv("CLAB_LABDIR_BASE"); base != "" {
295: 						candidates = append(candidates, filepath.Join(base, "clab-"+c.Config.Name))
296: 					}
297: 					if c.TopoPaths.TopologyFileIsSet() {
298: 						candidates = append(
299: 							candidates,
300: 							filepath.Join(c.TopoPaths.TopologyFileDir(), "clab-"+c.Config.Name),
301: 						)
302: 					} else {
303: 						if wd, err := os.Getwd(); err == nil && wd != "" {
304: 							candidates = append(
305: 								candidates,
306: 								filepath.Join(wd, "clab-"+c.Config.Name),
307: 							)
308: 						}
309: 					}
310: 					for _, cand := range candidates {
311: 						if _, err := os.Stat(cand); err == nil {
312: 							labDir = cand
313: 							break
314: 						}
315: 					}
316: 					if labDir == "" {
317: 						log.Info(
318: 							"lab directory not found, nothing to clean",
319: 							"candidates",
320: 							candidates,
321: 						)
322: 						return nil
323: 					}
324: 				} else {
325: 					log.Info("lab directory not found, nothing to clean")
326: 					return nil
327: 				}
328: 			}
329: 
330: 			// Safety: only remove directories that look like a lab directory.
331: 			base := filepath.Base(labDir)
332: 			if !strings.HasPrefix(base, "clab-") {
333: 				log.Warnf("refusing to remove lab directory %q: unexpected name", labDir)
334: 				return nil
335: 			}
336: 			if c.Config != nil && c.Config.Name != "" {
337: 				expected := "clab-" + c.Config.Name
338: 				if base != expected {
339: 					log.Warnf(
340: 						"refusing to remove lab directory %q: does not match expected %q",
341: 						labDir,
342: 						expected,
343: 					)
344: 					return nil
345: 				}
346: 			}
347: 
348: 			if _, err := os.Stat(labDir); os.IsNotExist(err) {
349: 				log.Info("lab directory not found, nothing to clean", "path", labDir)
350: 				return nil
351: 			} else if err != nil {
352: 				log.Debug("failed to stat lab directory, skipping", "path", labDir, "error", err)
353: 				return nil
354: 			}
355: 
356: 			log.Info("Removing lab directory", "path", labDir)
357: 			if err := os.RemoveAll(labDir); err != nil {
358: 				log.Errorf("error deleting lab directory: %v", err)
359: 				return err
360: 			}
361: 		}
362: 
363: 		return nil
364: 	}
365: 
366: 	for _, labdir := range topos {
367: 		if failedLabDirs[labdir] {
368: 			log.Warnf(
369: 				"keeping lab directory %s: the lab was not destroyed, so its state is kept for a later attempt",
370: 				labdir,
371: 			)
372: 
373: 			continue
374: 		}
375: 
376: 		err := os.RemoveAll(labdir)
377: 		if err != nil {
378: 			log.Errorf("error deleting lab directory: %v", err)
379: 		}
380: 	}
381: 
382: 	return nil
383: }

385: func (c *CLab) destroy(ctx context.Context, maxWorkers uint, keepMgmtNet bool) error {
386: 	var containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer
387: 	var orphanSidecars []clabruntime.GenericContainer
388: 	var err error
389: 
390: 	// If we have nodes defined (from topology file), list containers by node.
391: 	// Otherwise, list containers by lab name label (for destroy-by-name-only case).
392: 	if len(c.Nodes) > 0 {
393: 		containers, err = c.ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound(ctx)
394: 	} else if c.Config.Name != "" {
395: 		containers, err = c.ListContainers(ctx, WithListLabName(c.Config.Name))
396: 	}
397: 
398: 	if err != nil {
399: 		return err
400: 	}
401: 
402: 	if len(c.Nodes) == 0 {
403: 		c.addMgmtNetworksFromContainers(containers)
404: 	}
405: 
406: 	if len(c.Nodes) > 0 {
407: 		tailscaleContainers, err := c.discoverTailscaleContainers(ctx, c.nodeFilter)
408: 		if err != nil {
409: 			return err
410: 		}
411: 		for _, ctr := range tailscaleContainers {
412: 			if _, desired := c.Nodes[ctr.Labels[clabconstants.NodeName]]; desired {
413: 				continue
414: 			}
415: 			containers = append(containers, ctr)
416: 			if ctr.Labels[clabconstants.ToolType] == "" {
417: 				orphanSidecars = append(orphanSidecars, ctr)
418: 			}
419: 		}
420: 	}
421: 
422: 	if len(containers) == 0 {
423: 		if len(c.Nodes) > 0 && len(c.Links) > 0 {
424: 			c.deleteSpecialLinkNodes(ctx)
425: 		}
426: 		return nil
427: 	}
428: 
429: 	if maxWorkers == 0 {
430: 		maxWorkers = uint(len(containers))
431: 	}
432: 
433: 	log.Info("Destroying lab", "name", c.Config.Name)
434: 
435: 	// If we have nodes defined, use the normal node-based deletion.
436: 	// Otherwise, delete containers directly via the runtime (for destroy-by-name-only case).
437: 	if len(c.Nodes) > 0 {
438: 		c.preDestroyNodes(ctx, slices.Collect(maps.Values(c.Nodes)), maxWorkers)
439: 
440: 		err := clablinks.CleanupFilteredLinks(
441: 			ctx,
442: 			c.Config.Topology.Links,
443: 			c.Config.Name,
444: 			c.nodeFilter,
445: 		)
446: 		if err != nil {
447: 			return err
448: 		}
449: 		c.deleteNodes(ctx, maxWorkers)
450: 		c.deleteContainersDirect(ctx, orphanSidecars)
451: 	} else {
452: 		c.deleteContainersDirect(ctx, containers)
453: 	}
454: 
455: 	c.deleteToolContainers(ctx)
456: 
457: 	log.Info("Removing host entries", "path", "/etc/hosts")
458: 
459: 	err = c.DeleteEntriesFromHostsFile()
460: 	if err != nil {
461: 		return fmt.Errorf("error while trying to clean up the hosts file: %w", err)
462: 	}
463: 
464: 	log.Info("Removing SSH config", "path", c.TopoPaths.SSHConfigPath())
465: 
466: 	err = c.RemoveSSHConfig(c.TopoPaths)
467: 	if err != nil {
468: 		log.Errorf("failed to remove ssh config file: %v", err)
469: 	}
470: 
471: 	// delete container network namespaces symlinks
472: 	for _, node := range c.Nodes {
473: 		err = node.DeleteNetnsSymlink()
474: 		if err != nil {
475: 			return fmt.Errorf("error while deleting netns symlinks: %w", err)
476: 		}
477: 	}
478: 
479: 	// delete every defined management network, including extra networks
480: 	// that apply may have left without nodes, and networks a previous
481: 	// deployment recorded in the lab state but the topology no longer defines
482: 	for _, m := range c.mgmtNetworksForCleanup() {
483: 		if m.Network == "bridge" || keepMgmtNet {
484: 			continue
485: 		}
486: 		log.Debugf("Calling DeleteNet method. Management network value is: %+v", m)
487: 
488: 		rt, rtErr := c.mgmtRuntime(c.globalRuntimeName, m)
489: 		if rtErr != nil {
490: 			// runtimes without multiple network support never created extra networks
491: 			log.Debug("Skipping management network deletion", "network", m.Network, "error", rtErr)
492: 			continue
493: 		}
494: 		if err = rt.DeleteNet(ctx); err != nil {
495: 			switch {
496: 			case err.Error() == fmt.Sprintf("Error: No such network: %s", m.Network):
497: 			case strings.Contains(err.Error(), fmt.Sprintf(" network %s not found", m.Network)):
498: 			default:
499: 				log.Error(err)
500: 			}
501: 		}
502: 	}
503: 
504: 	return nil
505: }

507: func (c *CLab) addMgmtNetworksFromContainers(containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer) {
508: 	for _, ctr := range containers {
509: 		switch name := ctr.NetworkName; name {
510: 		case "", "unknown", "bridge", "host", "none":
511: 		default:
512: 			if c.mgmtNetByNetwork(name).Network == name {
513: 				continue
514: 			}
515: 			c.Config.MgmtNetworks = append(c.Config.MgmtNetworks, &clabtypes.MgmtNet{
516: 				Network:        name,
517: 				Bridge:         ctr.Labels[clabconstants.NodeMgmtNetBr],
518: 				ExternalAccess: new(true),
519: 			})
520: 		}
521: 	}
522: }
523: 
524: // mgmtNetworksForCleanup returns the management networks to delete on destroy:
525: // the topology-defined ones plus any network a previous deployment recorded in
526: // the lab state but that the current topology no longer defines. Without the
527: // state record a network dropped from the mgmt list would never be removed.
528: func (c *CLab) mgmtNetworksForCleanup() clabtypes.MgmtNetworks {
529: 	networks := c.allMgmtNetworks()
530: 
531: 	state, err := c.LoadState()
532: 	if err != nil {
533: 		log.Warn("Unable to load the management networks recorded in the lab state", "error", err)
534: 		return networks
535: 	}
536: 	if state == nil {
537: 		return networks
538: 	}
539: 
540: 	defined := make(map[string]bool, len(networks))
541: 	for _, m := range networks {
542: 		defined[m.Network] = true
543: 	}
544: 	for _, name := range state.MgmtNetworks {
545: 		if defined[name] {
546: 			continue
547: 		}
548: 		defined[name] = true
549: 		// ExternalAccess mirrors the default every management network gets, so
550: 		// the forwarding rule installed for the network is cleaned up too.
551: 		networks = append(networks, &clabtypes.MgmtNet{
552: 			Network:        name,
553: 			ExternalAccess: new(true),
554: 		})
555: 	}
556: 
557: 	return networks
558: }

560: func (c *CLab) deleteApplyNodes(ctx context.Context, plan *applyPlan) error {
561: 	nodeNames := make([]string, 0, len(plan.deletedNodeSet)+len(plan.recreatedNodeSet))
562: 	for nodeName := range plan.deletedNodeSet {
563: 		nodeNames = append(nodeNames, nodeName)
564: 	}
565: 	for nodeName := range plan.recreatedNodeSet {
566: 		nodeNames = append(nodeNames, nodeName)
567: 	}
568: 	sort.Strings(nodeNames)
569: 
570: 	hookNodes := make([]clabnodes.Node, 0, len(nodeNames))
571: 	var tailscaleContainers []clabruntime.GenericContainer
572: 	for _, nodeName := range nodeNames {
573: 		runtimeNode := plan.currentNodes[nodeName]
574: 		if runtimeNode == nil {
575: 			return fmt.Errorf("runtime node %q not found", nodeName)
576: 		}
577: 		if runtimeNode.external || runtimeNode.rootNamespaceBased {
578: 			continue
579: 		}
580: 		if len(runtimeNode.containers) > 0 &&
581: 			runtimeNode.containers[0].Labels[clabconstants.NodeKind] == clabnodestailscale.KindName {
582: 			tailscaleContainers = append(tailscaleContainers, runtimeNode.containers...)
583: 			continue
584: 		}
585: 		if node, ok := c.Nodes[nodeName]; ok {
586: 			hookNodes = append(hookNodes, node)
587: 		}
588: 	}
589: 	var logoutWg sync.WaitGroup
590: 	for _, ctr := range tailscaleContainers {
591: 		logoutWg.Go(func() { c.logoutTailscaleContainer(ctx, ctr) })
592: 	}
593: 	c.preDestroyNodes(ctx, hookNodes, 0)
594: 	logoutWg.Wait()
595: 
596: 	for _, nodeName := range nodeNames {
597: 		runtimeNode := plan.currentNodes[nodeName]
598: 		if runtimeNode.external || runtimeNode.rootNamespaceBased {
599: 			continue
600: 		}
601: 
602: 		for i := len(runtimeNode.containers) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
603: 			ctr := runtimeNode.containers[i]
604: 			if len(ctr.Names) == 0 {
605: 				return fmt.Errorf("runtime container for node %q has no name", nodeName)
606: 			}
607: 
608: 			runtime := ctr.Runtime
609: 			if runtime == nil {
610: 				runtime = c.globalRuntime()
611: 			}
612: 
613: 			action := "Deleting node"
614: 			if _, recreate := plan.recreatedNodeSet[nodeName]; recreate {
615: 				action = "Deleting node for recreate"
616: 			}
617: 			log.Info(action, "node", nodeName, "container", ctr.Names[0])
618: 			if err := runtime.DeleteContainer(ctx, ctr.Names[0]); err != nil {
619: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed deleting node %q: %w", nodeName, err)

629: // preDestroyNodes runs the PreDestroy stage of the given nodes concurrently, before any of them
630: // is deleted. Nodes without a container are skipped. A workers value of 0 runs all hooks at once.
631: func (*CLab) preDestroyNodes(ctx context.Context, nodes []clabnodes.Node, workers uint) {
632: 	if workers == 0 || workers > uint(len(nodes)) {
633: 		workers = uint(len(nodes))
634: 	}
635: 
636: 	sem := make(chan struct{}, workers)
637: 	wg := new(sync.WaitGroup)
638: 
639: 	for _, n := range nodes {
640: 		wg.Add(1)
641: 		sem <- struct{}{}
642: 
643: 		go func() {
644: 			defer wg.Done()
645: 			defer func() { <-sem }()
646: 
647: 			if n.GetContainerStatus(ctx) == clabruntime.NotFound {
648: 				return
649: 			}
650: 
651: 			if err := n.PreDestroy(ctx); err != nil {
652: 				log.Warnf("node %q pre-destroy hook failed: %v", n.Config().ShortName, err)
653: 			}
654: 		}()
655: 	}
656: 
657: 	wg.Wait()
658: }

660: func (c *CLab) deleteNodes(ctx context.Context, workers uint) {
661: 	wg := new(sync.WaitGroup)
662: 
663: 	concurrentChan := make(chan clabnodes.Node)
664: 
665: 	workerFunc := func(i uint, input chan clabnodes.Node, wg *sync.WaitGroup) {
666: 		defer wg.Done()
667: 
668: 		for {
669: 			select {
670: 			case n := <-input:
671: 				if n == nil {
672: 					log.Debugf("Worker %d terminating...", i)
673: 					return
674: 				}
675: 
676: 				err := n.Delete(ctx)
677: 				if err != nil {
678: 					log.Errorf("could not remove container %q: %v", n.Config().LongName, err)
679: 				}
680: 			case <-ctx.Done():
681: 				return
682: 			}
683: 		}
684: 	}
685: 
686: 	// start concurrent workers
687: 	wg.Add(int(workers))
688: 
689: 	for i := range workers {
690: 		go workerFunc(i, concurrentChan, wg)
691: 	}
692: 
693: 	// send nodes to workers
694: 	for _, n := range c.Nodes {
695: 		concurrentChan <- n
696: 	}
697: 
698: 	// close channel to terminate the workers
699: 	close(concurrentChan)
700: 
701: 	wg.Wait()
702: 
703: 	// Host and mgmt-br links must be removed only after node workers finish.
704: 	// vxlan-stitch teardown deletes veth pairs from containers concurrently with
705: 	// host-namespace VXLAN interfaces; running both at once races netlink deletes.
706: 	c.deleteSpecialLinkNodes(ctx)
707: }

712: 		clablinks.GetMgmtBrLinkNodes()...,
713: 	)
714: 	for _, n := range specialNodes {

716: 		if err != nil {
717: 			log.Warn(err)
718: 		}
719: 	}
720: }

744: 		}
745: 	}
746: }

# Karpathy behavioral guidelines

Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.

**Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.

## 1. Think Before Coding

**Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**

Before implementing:

- State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
- If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
- If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
- If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.

## 2. Simplicity First

**Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**

- No features beyond what was asked.
- No abstractions for single-use code.
- No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
- No error handling for impossible scenarios.
- If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.

Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.

## 3. Surgical Changes

**Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**

When editing existing code:

- Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
- Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
- Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
- If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.

When your changes create orphans:

- Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
- Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.

The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.

## 4. Goal-Driven Execution

**Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**

Transform tasks into verifiable goals:

- "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
- "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
- "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"

For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:

```
1. [Step] → verify: [check]
2. [Step] → verify: [check]
3. [Step] → verify: [check]
```

Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.

---

**These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.

31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"

34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.

OK. Now let me verify the diff context once more for correctness — particularly the `deleteNodes` change. In base, `wg.Wait()` was at the end after special node deletion. In head, `wg.Wait()` is right after `close(concurrentChan)`, then special node deletes. This means: workers finish before special nodes get deleted. That's the documented race fix.

One more consideration: `deleteSpecialLinkNodes` uses `log.Warn(err)` — charmbracelet log, fine.

Also check: is there anywhere else that relied on the old placement (special nodes deleted concurrently)? The extraction is clean.

For mgmt-net links, the bridge endpoint uses `r.HostInterface` (user-specified or default?) — if HostInterface is empty, iface name is empty. `EndpointGeneric.Remove` with empty iface name → `netlink.LinkByName("")` → likely error (not LinkNotFoundError) → `return err` → Delete returns err → `log.Warn`. Pre-existing behavior in the normal path too. Hmm — wait, for the normal destroy path with empty host-interface for mgmt-net link... the bridgeEp's iface name would be "" — but during deploy, the bridge endpoint is handled specially (veth attached to bridge). Remove for the bridgeEp with empty name... Let's check how the normal destroy path handles it — `GenericLinkNode.Delete` iterates endpoints, calls `l.Remove(ctx)` since l != nil (LinkVEth). Right! `e.GetLink()` is the LinkVEth, so `GenericLinkNode.Delete` calls `l.Remove(ctx)` (the link's Remove, which removes all endpoints) — not `e.Remove`. So it deletes both veth ends. Same for host links: `l.Remove` (LinkVEth.Remove). So the special node Delete mostly removes whole veth links. For stitched vxlan, host endpoint link is LinkVxlan → LinkVxlan.Remove. OK.

So in the early path, deleting special nodes removes whole veth links: container side (already gone) and host side (still present) — exactly the cleanup intended. And EndpointGeneric.Remove tolerates not-found interfaces. Good.

Now, is there any issue with `LinkVEth.Remove` being invoked from two places concurrently...? In the early path, no concurrency. In deleteNodes path, special deletes happen after wg.Wait — sequential. But there's a remaining concurrency: node workers each call `n.Delete(ctx)` → for each endpoint `e.GetLink().Remove(ctx)`. Two endpoints of the same veth belong to two different nodes → two workers could call Remove on the SAME LinkVEth concurrently → deployMutex guards. Pre-existing.

OK. So the change is sound. Now findings:

1. Possibly P4: missing explanatory comment for the new early-return call site, and/or the redundant-looking guard. Hmm, is that worth a finding? The instructions want actionable clarity findings only when there's concrete maintenance cost. The condition `len(c.Nodes) > 0 && len(c.Links) > 0` at the early return is non-obvious: `c.Links` is a proxy for "special link nodes may hold endpoints". A reader may wonder why Links>0 matters. A one-line comment would help. I'll make it a P4.

2. Coverage: no unit test for the new early-return path. The fake runtime harness (`listEmptyAfterFirst`) plus a topology with a host link could exercise it, but asserting the netlink delete requires a seam. Hmm. Could assert behaviorally? Not easily. I'll put it in coverage notes, not a finding.

3. Anything else? Let me reconsider the ordering comment claim: "Host and mgmt-br links must be removed only after node workers finish." Is wg.Wait placement before special deletes definitively fixing a race? In base, the special node delete ran concurrently with node workers. For vxlan-stitch: node worker deletes container-side endpoints → `e.GetLink().Remove(ctx)`. What's the container endpoint's link for a stitched vxlan? The veth component's container endpoint: created via `r.Endpoint.Resolve(params, link)` inside `LinkHostRaw.Resolve` where link is the LinkVEth — so container endpoint's link is the vethLink (LinkVEth). Its Remove deletes both veth ends (container + host ve- iface). The vxlan endpoint (vx- iface) is on the host node with link = LinkVxlan (since resolveLocalEndpoint passes `link` = the LinkVxlan). So host node Delete → LinkVxlan.Remove → deletes vx- interface in host ns.

In base: worker A deletes vethLink (both ends) while host node delete deletes vx- interface. Is there a race? `stitch()` sets up TC filters between the veth and vxlan. Deleting the veth while deleting the vxlan concurrently — kernel-level, probably fine, but netlink operations in the same netns... Actually the race is plausibly: LinkVxlan.Remove and LinkVEth.Remove both touch the host netns; the veth delete may... Honestly, the PR author documented the race; I can't disprove it. The fix is reasonable either way (serializing is safe).

Hmm, wait — actually there's a subtlety I should double check: does `LinkVxlan.Remove` also remove the vxlan's host-side? And is the vxlan endpoint attached to the host singleton via AddEndpoint? `NewEndpointVxlan(params.Nodes["host"], link)` — `params.Nodes["host"]` is the host link node (from getSpecialLinkNodes). Then AddEndpoint — is it called? In `LinkHostRaw.Resolve` it's explicitly called for hostEp. For vxlanRawEp.Resolve — check EndpointRaw.Resolve for host node type: it probably calls AddEndpoint too. Let me verify quickly to confirm the host node's Delete iterates vxlan endpoints (thus the serialization matters).

But consider `Destroy` (outer) looping over multiple topos sequentially: for topo1, copy1 resolved → attach; copy1.destroy → special deletes → endpoints removed (netlink) but remain in the singleton's slice (Remove doesn't prune). For topo2, copy2's ResolveLinks → resetResolvedLinks releases only copy2's (empty) endpoints → attaches copy2's endpoints → singleton now has [copy1's stale, copy2's]. copy2's deleteSpecialLinkNodes deletes all: copy1's stale → Remove → LinkVEth.Remove: DeploymentState == Removed? copy1's Remove succeeded → state Removed → returns nil immediately. Only when copy1's Remove FAILED does re-attempt occur — and a retry that succeeds now removes an interface that may have been legitimately re-created by a re-deployed lab with the same name. Edge of edge. Pre-existing pattern. Skip.

Hmm, is that too weak? "Flag confusing control flow or naming when you can explain a concrete maintenance or correctness cost." I think a comment suggestion is fair as P4.

Alternatively suggest: make `deleteSpecialLinkNodes` accept the nodes so a test can pass fake nodes... that changes signature. Actually, wait. Maybe a better testable observation: with the existing `TestDestroyCleanupRemovesLabDirsOnSuccess` harness (listEmptyAfterFirst), if the topo had a host link, the new code path would run `deleteSpecialLinkNodes`. I'll keep it as coverage note, not a finding. Per instructions: "Recommend the smallest useful check for a concrete gap" — the gap is real (the race fix ordering is untested, and the early path is untested). But given both require netlink or refactoring, a coverage note is honest. Actually, I can suggest ONE small check: refactor-free — a unit test for the guard semantics is trivial if `deleteSpecialLinkNodes` took the specialNodes slice... I'll put it in coverage notes with a suggestion.

Skip (pre-existing; per scope "Focus on issues introduced or materially worsened by this PR").

## Code Review: `core/destroy.go` — clean up special link nodes when containers are already gone

### ScopeThe PR makes two changes, both in `core/destroy.go`:

1. When `destroy()` finds no lab containers at all (topology loaded, containers already removed), it now still calls the new `deleteSpecialLinkNodes(ctx)` before returning, gated by `len(c.Nodes) > 0 && len(c.Links) > 0` ([head `core/destroy.go:422-427`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/391b213e646cd3b00d9e9711313d53782e8d0c82/core/destroy.go#L422-L427)).
2. In `deleteNodes()`, `wg.Wait()` is moved before special-node deletion, and the special-node loop is extracted into `deleteSpecialLinkNodes` ([head `core/destroy.go:696-720`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/391b213e646cd3b00d9e9711313d53782e8d0c82/core/destroy.go#L696-L720)). This serializes node-worker teardown (which deletes container-side veth ends and the veth components of stitched links) with the host/mgmt-br node teardown (which deletes host-namespace interfaces, notably the `vx-*` VXLAN devices).

### Verification performed

- **Correctness of the early-return guard.** `c.Links` is only populated by `makeCopyForDestroy` → `ResolveLinks()` (called by both the `Destroy` command path at `core/destroy.go:122` and the `--reconfigure` path at `core/deploy.go:190-198`), so `len(c.Links) > 0` is a sound proxy for "this lab's resolved links attached endpoints to the shared host/mgmt-br nodes". Both call sites always pass through `ResolveLinks`, so the guard cannot skip cleanup that is needed. `len(nil map)` is 0, so an unloaded topology is safe. The guard is not a strict necessity (special-node `Delete` is a no-op with no endpoints), but it avoids needless netlink probing, especially for the stale-endpoint case noted below.
- **Correctness of the extracted helper.** `deleteSpecialLinkNodes` is a pure extraction of the former in-`deleteNodes` loop: same `GetHostLinkNode()` + `GetMgmtBrLinkNodes()` list, same `log.Warn` on failure. All three references (early return at line 424, call at 706, definition at 709) are within this file.
- **Idempotency of the cleanup.** `GenericLinkNode.Delete` iterates endpoints and calls `e.GetLink().Remove(ctx)`; `LinkVEth.Remove`, `LinkVxlan.Remove` and `LinkVEthStitched.Remove` are all idempotent via the `LinkDeploymentStateRemoved` guard (`links/link.go:26-32`), and `EndpointGeneric.Remove` treats `LinkNotFoundError` as success. So a second invocation (e.g., from a reconfigure destroy, or from a subsequent lab in a `destroy --all` process) is a harmless no-op.
- **Why the early path matters.** Host-namespace veth endpoints (host links, mgmt-net bridge ends, veth-stitch far ends) die together with the container netns, so they cannot linger after container removal. The `vx-*` VXLAN devices created for `vxlan-stitch` links live in the host netns independently of any container and *do* survive out-of-band container removal — which matches the class of leftover this fix addresses. The fix scope is internally consistent.
- **Node filter interaction.** Filtered-out links never attach endpoints during `ResolveLinks`, so a filtered destroy with `containers == 0` correctly deletes only the artifacts of the filtered-in nodes.
- **`deleteContainersDirect` path** (destroy-by-name-only, `c.Nodes == 0`) is untouched; the new guard correctly excludes it via `len(c.Nodes) > 0`.

I found no correctness, performance, schema, or documentation defect introduced by this change. Two small, optional improvements follow.

### Findings

#### P4 — Document why the early-return path deletes special link nodes

- **Location:** [head `core/destroy.go:422-427`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/391b213e646cd3b00d9e9711313d53782e8d0c82/core/destroy.go#L422-L427)
- **Problem:** The new guard `len(c.Nodes) > 0 && len(c.Links) > 0` encodes non-obvious invariants: `c.Links` is populated only by `ResolveLinks()` inside `makeCopyForDestroy`, and it is the only signal that this lab's resolved links attached endpoints to the process-wide host/mgmt-br singleton nodes. Nothing at the call site explains why a "no containers" destroy performs cleanup at all, or why the `c.Links` condition is there. This file is otherwise heavily commented in exactly these places (see the new comment added at `core/destroy.go:703-705`), so the omission stands out.
- **Trigger:** Any future maintainer reading or refactoring `destroy()` — for example someone may drop the `len(c.Links) > 0` condition as redundant, or wonder whether cleanup with zero containers is safe.
- **Impact:** Maintenance cost only; behavior is correct as written.
- **Suggestion:** Add a two-line comment above the guard, e.g. "containers may have been removed out-of-band, but host-namespace artifacts of resolved links (notably `vx-*` VXLAN devices of vxlan-stitch links) survive them; clean up the special link nodes when this lab resolved any links". Optionally cross-reference the comment in `deleteNodes`.

#### P4 — No runnable check covers the new cleanup path or the teardown ordering

- **Location:** [head `core/destroy.go:696-720`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/391b213e646cd3b00d9e9711313d53782e8d0c82/core/destroy.go#L696-L720); existing harness at `core/destroy_test.go:216-388`
- **Problem:** Both behavioral changes — deleting special link nodes when containers are already gone, and running special-node deletion only after `wg.Wait()` — are untested. The repo already has a cheap fake-runtime harness for `destroy()` (`fakeDestroyRuntime`, `registerDestroyTestRuntime`, `writeDestroyTestTopology` in `core/destroy_test.go`), so the early-return path is reachable without a container runtime.
- **Trigger:** A regression that reverts either change (e.g., a refactor moving `deleteSpecialLinkNodes` back before `wg.Wait()`, or dropping the early-return call) would pass the current test suite.
- **Impact:** Unprotected fix for a race and a leftover-artifact bug; both are exactly the kind of behavior that silently regresses.
- **Suggestion:** Add one test reusing the existing harness: write a topology whose single node has a `host:` link endpoint, set `destroyTestBehavior` with an empty container list, run `Destroy`, and assert that the link attached to the singleton `clablinks.GetHostLinkNode().GetEndpoints()[0].GetLink()` reaches `LinkDeploymentStateRemoved`. The interfaces do not exist in the test environment, so `Remove` is a harmless logging no-op, and the zero value `LinkDeploymentStateNotDeployed` distinguishes the old behavior (no deletion). This pins the early-return path without any netlink or runtime dependency; the `wg.Wait()` ordering is harder to assert without a seam and can reasonably remain covered by review.

### Coverage notes

- Review is source-only; no tests or code were executed. Coverage is complete for the changed file and its callers (`core/destroy.go:122`, `core/deploy.go:190-198`), the link-lifecycle helpers backing the cleanup (`links/link.go`, `links/generic_link_node.go`, `links/endpoint.go`, `links/link_host.go`, `links/link_mgmt-net.go`, `links/link_veth.go`, `links/link_vxlan.go`, `links/link_vxlan_stitched.go`), and the existing test harness.
- Pre-existing behaviors observed but not introduced or materially worsened by this PR, hence not filed as findings: process-wide singleton link nodes can accumulate stale endpoints from a previous lab whose destroy failed before `deleteNodes` (mitigated in the common case by the `LinkDeploymentStateRemoved` idempotency guard); the `deleteNodes` sender loop can deadlock on `concurrentChan` if the context is cancelled after workers exit; the early return still skips `sshx`/`gotty` tool-container cleanup.
